lnq_atlas.description: Segments visible mediastinal lymph-node candidates on one CT series. The output is one aggregate ROI, Mediastinal_Lymph_Node_Candidate, not an elective nodal region or a station map. No remaining candidate completes with no RTSTRUCT.
lnq_atlas.limitations: Code licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Archive weight terms are not stated. Owner accepted these terms on 2026-10-22. The installed adapter uses the challenge-submission post-processing: binarization threshold 0.3 and a 5 mm minimum diameter. This task is routed to the H100 worker. On the P6000 portal (compute capability 6.1), keep lnq_atlas in REMOTE_GPU_TASKS. An acceptance marker recorded on the H100 does not enable the task on a P6000. H100 acceptance passed on 2026-10-22 on a public CT (MSD Task06 lung_053): two production runs and the released predictor gave identical masks (17,234 voxels). Selectable only after the GPU acceptance marker and the orientation marker pass.
lnq_atlas.evidence_note: Engelson et al., MELBA 2024, sections 4.1-4.3 and Tables 2 and 4, on the LNQ test set of 100 patients and 861 reference nodes. The ablation that uses all modifications, a binarization threshold of 0.2 and no minimum-diameter filter had Dice 0.6033 and found 57% of reference nodes (LN-found 0.5654), compared with 27% (LN-found 0.2749) when training on CT only. The challenge submission, a five-model ensemble with threshold 0.3 and a 5 mm minimum diameter, had Dice 0.5690 and ASSD 6.8976 mm on that same test set. The authors state that post-processing fit on the small validation set did not carry over to the test set. The installed adapter uses the submission settings, not the 0.2 ablation.

biomedparse_prompted.description: BiomedParse v2 segments one supported text-selected organ, lesion or other target from one CT, MR or PET series. It returns one ROI named from that target, with per-slice existence scores and the foreground voxel count. An existence-negative result is reported as object not detected.
biomedparse_prompted.limitations: Research and development use only; not for clinical decisions. Owner accepted these terms on 2026-10-22. One prompt-selected target, which may have several disconnected components; not an elective nodal atlas. Only documented modality-specific targets are accepted. CT uses the README window for the selected anatomy; MR and PET use 0.5–99.5 percentile clipping, with no SUV conversion. The authors do not publish how they converted their v2 training images to 8-bit or which window they used for their AMOS example, so our raw-image normalization follows the README but is not confirmed to match their training data. Runs on the H100 only: on 2026-10-25 it matched the authors' unmodified inference exactly on their public AMOS spleen example, and that example, stored as raw HU in synthetic DICOM geometry, produced a validated RTSTRUCT. That check covers our conversion and contour geometry, not accuracy. No P6000 acceptance exists. Not tested on patient data.
biomedparse_prompted.evidence_note: The Nature Methods 2025 paper describes v1: Extended Data Fig. 4 reports better segmentation than SegVol across 27,779 CT target samples (paired test p < 2.23×10^-308). This is not a v2 volumetric result. The BoltzFormer author preprint (arXiv:2503.02841v2; CVPR 2025 paper), Table 1 and Appendix B, reports mean Dice 75.4% for Focal-L on 1,733 LIDC-IDRI nodule samples, versus 73.8% for pretrained BiomedParse. These are processed 2D benchmark samples, not patients, and do not establish the accuracy of the released v2 3D checkpoint. The v2 README reports first place in the CVPR 2025 challenge; challenge score and evaluation cohort remain unverified.
